properties.Name: Lake Merritt United Methodist Church
properties.Short_Description: This is our Starting point and Ending point.
properties.Description_1: This site also marks where I first met Tom, who has been involved in this program for over ten years and has coordinated the route since the onset of COVID-19 (2020). Volunteers assemble here to load the carts with lunches, typically five wagons, including one with hygiene supplies and four with sandwiches.
properties.Description_2:
The lunch bags generally contain one sandwich, one egg, a small bottle of water, one to two apples, and assorted snacks. We typically distribute two bags per person.

*Additional information is available on the organization’s website linked below the map title.

properties.Name: First Stop
properties.Short_Description: First stop, an encampment under the bridge
properties.Description_1: According to Tom, approximately 7–8 individuals reside in this encampment, which spans the length of the underpass. Five months ago, the area was more open, but recently it has become more enclosed. Volunteers call out “Lake Lunches” near the entrance; usually one or two residents come out, share how many people are inside, and we leave the appropriate number of lunches at the entrance.

properties.Name: Second Stop
properties.Description_1: This location typically includes a couple and several individuals seated along the stone slabs. People approach us directly, and we distribute lunches accordingly. I have the chance to chat with the couple some times, they mentioned that they are not trying to apply for housing but the different documents and the tedious process is very hard to sit through.
properties.Description_2: Tom also offers donated jackets or winter clothing here. He mentioned they often prioritize distributing clothing to individuals living in tents.

properties.Name: Small Stop - The Benches
properties.Description_1: This location is a known gathering spot. Visual cues—such as shoes hanging from the power line—often signal informal meeting areas. Volunteers approach this spot with awareness while offering lunches. Individuals here tend to take lunches less frequently than at other stops.

properties.Name: Small Stop - The Grassland
properties.Description_1: We typically meet several individuals here accompanied by four dogs. The owners are always eager to introduce them. Although the dogs may bark initially, they quickly become friendly once prompted by their owners.
properties.Description_2: One of the dogs, a white dog named Diamond, is well known. The others’ names are not known. Tom mentioned this group is relatively new to the area.

properties.Name: Small Stop - Camron-Stanford House
properties.Description_1: Ms. Chen is frequently present in this area. She cares for her husband at home and is consistently appreciative of the volunteers. From observation, she has developed close relationships with several long-term volunteers and often greets them with hugs.

properties.Name: Thrid Stop
properties.Short_Description: Oakland Public Library, one of our bigger stops
properties.Description_1: Some individuals exit the library to receive lunches, and the area appears to be a common place where people spend time.
properties.Description_2: Tom shared that the library has expressed concerns about distributing food directly in front of the building, possibly due to issues like crumbs or waste. As a result, volunteers now stop across the street in front of the Alameda County Administration Building.

properties.Name: Small Stop - Garage
properties.Description_1: This is a newer addition to the route. When I first joined the volunteer group, we did not stop here. It is generally a brief and quiet stop.

properties.Name: Small Stop - Hill Castle Apartments
properties.Short_Description: sometimes there is a lady waiting for us here
properties.Description_1: According to Tom, this woman also cares for her husband at home.

properties.Name: Fourth Stop
properties.Description_1: Residents often come outside to receive lunches. Afterwards, remaining lunches (typically 6–7) are left at the hotel’s front desk.
properties.Description_2: Upon doing a little bit research online, this place is a senior caring facility, though might not be a good one. One yelp review  from 2014 quote " they get two meals a day and nothing on weekends". Tom explained that earlier versions of the route focused only on Lake Merritt, but the previous organizer added this stop after learning that residents here sometimes have housing but still lack adequate living conditions.
